HPEB 300.description: Advanced skills in planning, implementing, and evaluating community health promotion programs to foster behavior changes in high-risk groups and enhance health outcomes. Examination and application of the PRECEDE-PROCEED Model, an evidence-based conceptual framework, to strategically plan targeted and focused public health programs.
HPEB 300.subject: HPEB
HPEB 300.title: Planning Health Promotion Programs

HPEB 301.description: Practical experience in applying health promotion principles in the community or organization.
HPEB 301.subject: HPEB
HPEB 301.title: Practicum in Health Promotion

HPEB 321.description: Psychosocial health, stress management, leading infectious and noninfectious diseases, nutrition, physical fitness, sexuality, consumer health and health care access, environmental health, aging, and death.
HPEB 321.subject: HPEB
HPEB 321.title: Personal and Community Health

HPEB 331.description: Methods and materials for elementary schools. Integration and correlation of materials with school subjects. Sample content developed for primary, intermediate, and upper grades.
HPEB 331.subject: HPEB
HPEB 331.title: Health Education for the Elementary School

HPEB 335.description: Emphasis upon preparing school personnel to act responsibly in emergency situations. Includes the American National Red Cross standard and advanced first aid instruction.
HPEB 335.subject: HPEB
HPEB 335.title: First Aid and Emergency Preparedness

HPEB 399.description: Enrollment and topic to be approved in advance by advisor and instructor. Open to sophomores and above.
HPEB 399.subject: HPEB
HPEB 399.title: Independent Study

HPEB 434.description: Methods of teaching health in school and community settings; techniques and strategies.
HPEB 434.subject: HPEB
HPEB 434.title: Health Education

HPEB 468.description: Place of safety in modern life. Contributing factors to accidents, developing an awareness of the potential accident situation with special emphasis upon school setting, planning for and conduct of a safety education program.
HPEB 468.subject: HPEB
HPEB 468.title: Safety and Safety Education

HPEB 470.description: Examination of major global health topics and approaches used by governmental, non-governmental, international institutions and donor agencies to improve health in low and middle income countries. Critical analysis and generation of intervention strategies to combat health issues in various country settings.
HPEB 470.subject: HPEB
HPEB 470.title: Principles of Global Health

HPEB 471.description: The social, cultural, economic, and political factors that influence health and its distribution within and between populations. How society helps shape our health beliefs, behaviors, and status.
HPEB 471.subject: HPEB
HPEB 471.title: Social Determinants of Health

HPEB 488.description: Multiple dimensions of food systems along multiple dimensions of theory and practice. Restricted to Junior or Senior level standing.
HPEB 488.subject: HPEB
HPEB 488.title: Food Systems

HPEB 489.description: Synthesis and application of content and competencies of the minor in nutrition and food systems in a practical setting with emphasis on student identified areas for professional growth. Restricted to Senior level standing.
HPEB 489.subject: HPEB
HPEB 489.title: Food Systems Capstone Seminar

HPEB 492.description: A study of special topics in health promotion, education, and behavior. Individual topics to be announced in master schedule by title.
HPEB 492.subject: HPEB
HPEB 492.title: Special Topics in Health Promotion, Education, and Behavior

HPEB 501.description: Planning, implementation and evaluation of effective sexuality education programs. Includes strategies for educating about a variety of sexuality topics (e.g., reproductive biology, relationships, HIV/AIDS, sexual orientation, pregnancy, childbirth, and parenting).
HPEB 501.subject: HPEB
HPEB 501.title: Human Sexuality Education

HPEB 502.description: Application of nutrition principles including functions of food and nutrients in health and disease prevention throughout the life cycle. Applied topics include weight management, food safety, and other contemporary issues.
HPEB 502.subject: HPEB
HPEB 502.title: Applied Aspects of Human Nutrition

HPEB 511.description: Promoting individual and community health in an ever-changing society with a focus on prevention.
HPEB 511.subject: HPEB
HPEB 511.title: Health Promotion in a Changing Society

HPEB 512.description: Investigation of the unique health and disease profile of the American South, including regional disparities that remain unresolved despite a public health revolution. Topics range from endemic diseases of the antebellum period to the current HIV/AIDS crisis, and ethics of research.
HPEB 512.subject: HPEB
HPEB 512.title: Southern Discomfort: Public Health in the American South

HPEB 513.description: A comprehensive overview of race/ethnicity and health. Class discussions will focus on comparing health status and health outcomes of different racial/ethnic groups in the U.S. and discussing possible explanations for inequalities from a behavioral science perspective.
HPEB 513.subject: HPEB
HPEB 513.title: Race, Ethnicity, and Health: Examining Health Inequalities

HPEB 521.description: A course designed to acquaint the student with the various facets of the modern school health program. Includes school responsibilities for health and safety instruction, school health services, school environmental health problems, school and community relationships, resources for health, and evaluation of programs.
HPEB 521.subject: HPEB
HPEB 521.title: The Total School Health Program

HPEB 540.description: Nature of drug actions, motivational factors that influence the use and abuse of drugs, and examination and evaluation of procedures to provide effective drug prevention efforts.
HPEB 540.subject: HPEB
HPEB 540.title: Drug Prevention

HPEB 542.description: Examines policies and practices for tobacco prevention and control in public health.
HPEB 542.subject: HPEB
HPEB 542.title: Tobacco Prevention and Control in Public Health

HPEB 547.description: An analysis and appraisal of issues related to the production and distribution of products and services as these activities affect consumer health.
HPEB 547.subject: HPEB
HPEB 547.title: Consumer Health in Contemporary Society

HPEB 550.description: The development of interpersonal skills in dealing with health clients in various settings.
HPEB 550.subject: HPEB
HPEB 550.title: Behavioral Concepts and Processes for the Health Professional

HPEB 551.description: Application of observation techniques, field notes, informant interviewing, and secondary data analysis to interpreting differential perceptions of health problem solving in the community and clinic.
HPEB 551.subject: HPEB
HPEB 551.title: Medical Anthropology: Fieldwork

HPEB 552.description: Socio-cultural factors in health, illness, healing, and in medical systems. Cross-cultural and ethnographic evidence for public health research and program applications.
HPEB 552.subject: HPEB
HPEB 552.title: Medical Anthropology

HPEB 553.description: Identification and analysis of community health issues, their causes, and the roles of individuals, community agencies, and government in affecting their solutions. Emphasis upon personal involvement and responsibility for community health.
HPEB 553.subject: HPEB
HPEB 553.title: Community Health

HPEB 555.description: Conceptualizing the nature of the stress; psychological, emotional, and spiritual aspects of stress; competency in the active management of stress and mobilizing support.
HPEB 555.subject: HPEB
HPEB 555.title: Managing Stress

HPEB 560.description: The role of food in defining our relationships to our family, community, nation, and world. How food underlies much of the political, economic, and social struggles throughout the world.
HPEB 560.subject: HPEB
HPEB 560.title: Cooking Up a Storm: Food, Globalization, Localization, and Health in the South

HPEB 602.description: A study of health program and policy implementation processes and activities, illustrating how implementation can be the object of study in both general and intervention-specific research.
HPEB 602.subject: HPEB
HPEB 602.title: Implementation Science of Health Promotion Interventions

HPEB 620.description: Examination of nutritional concerns, requirements, and metabolism from pre-conception through the aging process; analysis of cultural, environmental, psychosocial, physical, and economic factors affecting nutritional status through the life cycle; and methods for assuring adequate nutrition through dietary selection, promotion of healthy eating throughout the life cycle and nutritional assessment for each state of the life cycle.
HPEB 620.subject: HPEB
HPEB 620.title: Nutrition Through the Life Cycle

HPEB 621.description: Public health issues, social and behavioral science, policies, programs, and services related to maternal and child health in the United States and other countries.
HPEB 621.subject: HPEB
HPEB 621.title: Maternal and Child Health

HPEB 627.description: Health status and concerns of lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender communities. Includes an examination of measurement issues and methodological considerations in research, as well as intervention efforts targeting LGBT populations.
HPEB 627.subject: HPEB
HPEB 627.title: Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual and Transgender (LGBT) Health

HPEB 631.description: A multimedia course emphasizing health education strategies for major S.C. health problems, risk factors, and concepts of positive health behavior.
HPEB 631.subject: HPEB
HPEB 631.title: Health Promotion for Elementary and Middle School Teachers

HPEB 640.description: The ways behavioral economics can help achieve goals in public health and health care. How behavioral insights can be applied to reach promotion aims ranging from achieving weight loss to medication adherence to appointment attendance.
HPEB 640.subject: HPEB
HPEB 640.title: Behavioral Economics in Public Health

HPEB 653.description: Assessment of nutritional outcomes and work with research participants/patients. Methods for collection of dietary data, anthropometry, and body composition, including the use of new technologies. Nutrition counseling and interviewing techniques useful in gathering nutrition information.
HPEB 653.subject: HPEB
HPEB 653.title: Nutrition Assessment and Counseling

HPEB 654.description: A survey of current concepts in clinical and public health nutrition which are unique to infants, children, and pregnant and lactating women.
HPEB 654.subject: HPEB
HPEB 654.title: Maternal and Child Nutrition

HPEB 674.description: Examination of health sciences and sociological research on social networks, social capital, and health. Theoretical and methodological foundations for network analysis of social relationships and health, design of public health interventions, and use of online social networks to promote health. Key constructs include social support, social capital, and social diffusion.
HPEB 674.subject: HPEB
HPEB 674.title: Social Networks, Social Capital, and Health

HPEB 679.description: Approaches for prevention of childhood obesity, using perspectives from public health, social work, exercise science, pharmacy, medicine, and behavioral nutrition. Training to teach diet/physical activity lessons in elementary school settings.
HPEB 679.subject: HPEB
HPEB 679.title: Addressing Childhood Obesity through Community Approaches

HPEB 680.description: Practical laboratory skills and theoretical bases of measurements in human physiology; bioelectrical potentials, respiratory physiology, energy expenditure, body composition, temperature regulation, and biochemical assays.
HPEB 680.subject: HPEB
HPEB 680.title: Laboratory Techniques in Physiological Measurement

HPEB 683.description: Overview of sexual health. Topics include sexual health across the life span, critical issues in sexual health, and sexual health interventions.
HPEB 683.subject: HPEB
HPEB 683.title: Sexual Health

HPEB 684.description: The role of effective behavioral interventions in preventing the spread of the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and other sexually transmitted infections (STI) among diverse populations.
HPEB 684.subject: HPEB
HPEB 684.title: HIV/STI Prevention

HPEB 690.description: Topics to be assigned and approved by advisor and department head.
HPEB 690.subject: HPEB
HPEB 690.title: Independent Study

HPEB 701.description: Role of theory in shaping research and practice in health promotion and education; historical and ongoing interaction between health education and the applied social sciences.
HPEB 701.subject: HPEB
HPEB 701.title: Theoretical Foundations of Health Promotion

HPEB 702.description: Health promotion planning frameworks; issues in planning, implementing, and evaluating health promotion programs in a variety of settings.
HPEB 702.subject: HPEB
HPEB 702.title: Planning Health Promotion Programs

HPEB 703.description: An examination of controversial and critical issues confronting the health educator, including ethical and professional concerns relating to the practice of health education in a variety of settings.
HPEB 703.subject: HPEB
HPEB 703.title: Public Health Education Seminar

HPEB 704.description: Presentation and discussion of research topics in health education. May be repeated for up to a total of 3 hours.
HPEB 704.subject: HPEB
HPEB 704.title: Health Education Research Seminar

HPEB 705.description: This course will explore and analyze various concepts of health, disease, and illness as applicable to health education. Consideration will be given to alternative concepts of health and their implications for directions in health education.
HPEB 705.subject: HPEB
HPEB 705.title: Contemporary Concepts of Health and Health Education

HPEB 706.description: Consultation for role, program, and organization development in local and state health agencies, and in communities. Advanced practice in consulting roles aimed at system change.
HPEB 706.subject: HPEB
HPEB 706.title: Consultation in Health Systems

HPEB 707.description: Research methods applicable to the study of individual and group health behavior. Interfaces behavioral theory, research design and methods, and data analysis/interpretation. Introduction to evaluating health promotion research and evaluation.
HPEB 707.subject: HPEB
HPEB 707.title: Health Promotion Research Methods

HPEB 708.description: Curricular planning and instructional strategies utilized in public health education settings.
HPEB 708.subject: HPEB
HPEB 708.title: Health Education Methods

HPEB 709.description: Identifies environmental, organizational, interpersonal, and individual patterns of stress with particular reference to health professionals; competency in the active management of stress and mobilizing support in health settings and organizations is evaluated.
HPEB 709.subject: HPEB
HPEB 709.title: Stress and Support Concepts and Management

HPEB 710.description: Planning and implementation of health education program evaluations. Emphasis on political, practical, and theoretical aspects of evaluation.
HPEB 710.subject: HPEB
HPEB 710.title: Evaluation of Health Promotion Programs

HPEB 711.description: Application of communication, media, and health behavior theory to the development of health communication messages and campaigns.
HPEB 711.subject: HPEB
HPEB 711.title: Applied Health Communication

HPEB 712.description: Students plan and implement a class on changing a health practice such as exercise, diet, or smoking. Lectures and reading assignments on theoretical foundations of how to conduct classes in changing health practices.
HPEB 712.subject: HPEB
HPEB 712.title: Changing Health Practices

HPEB 713.description: Psychosocial and behavioral factors in physical activity. Topics include mental health effects of exercise, behavior change theories applied to mental health effects of exercise, behavior change theories applied to physical activity, and physical activity determinants and interventions.
HPEB 713.subject: HPEB
HPEB 713.title: Behavioral Aspects of Physical Activity

HPEB 715.description: An overview of qualitative data collection and analysis methods commonly used in public health research with an emphasis on practical applications and hands-on experience.
HPEB 715.subject: HPEB
HPEB 715.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Public Health

HPEB 720.description: For persons administratively responsible for the school health program and for individuals involved in discharging the various responsibilities. Characteristics of the Health Education Coordinator; areas of responsibility, policies and procedures relative to health education needs; curricular patterns; criteria for an extensive evaluation of selected school health programs.
HPEB 720.subject: HPEB
HPEB 720.title: Coordinating the School Health Program

HPEB 722.description: The basis and nature of the health curriculum, its development, and appraisal of state and national health education curricula.
HPEB 722.subject: HPEB
HPEB 722.title: Health Education Curriculum Development

HPEB 723.description: Drivers, manifestations, measurement, and impacts of stigma on various disease conditions among diverse populations. Includes application of knowledge and skills to critically review interventions aiming to reduce stigma or mitigate the negative impacts of stigma.
HPEB 723.subject: HPEB
HPEB 723.title: Stigma and Public Health

HPEB 726.description: Design and implementation of community-based educational practices and services to prevent teen pregnancy.
HPEB 726.subject: HPEB
HPEB 726.title: Prevention of Teen Pregnancy

HPEB 730.description: Knowledge and skills for identifying needs, obtaining support, designing curricula, organizing resources, training personnel, implementing activities, and evaluating patient education programs are presented.
HPEB 730.subject: HPEB
HPEB 730.title: Programs for Patient Education

HPEB 731.description: Research and practice issues in health promotion with older adults, including the impact of ageism, ethnicity, gender, normal aging changes, self-management skills, and social networks on healthy aging.
HPEB 731.subject: HPEB
HPEB 731.title: Health Promotion for Older Adults

HPEB 742.description: Public health policy issues related to treatment, prevention, research, and education in the field of alcohol and drug abuse.
HPEB 742.subject: HPEB
HPEB 742.title: Alcohol, Drugs, and Public Health Policy

HPEB 748.description: Organizational development, policy influence, capacity building, empowerment, community diagnosis and coalition development for enhancing health.
HPEB 748.subject: HPEB
HPEB 748.title: Community Health Development

HPEB 750.description: Causative agents of chronic disease, with particular emphasis placed on those illnesses which have been termed psychosomatic and related to or caused by stress; physiological response of the individual to contemporary psychological stressors as well as methods of adaptation and prophylaxis.
HPEB 750.subject: HPEB
HPEB 750.title: Health Implications of Stress and Disease

HPEB 751.description: An examination of physical activity/exercise habit patterns as they relate to health status. Emphasis on the chronic effects of exercise.
HPEB 751.subject: HPEB
HPEB 751.title: Physical Activity and Health

HPEB 752.description: A study of the relationship of human nutrition to public health and the potential for risk reduction through health education.
HPEB 752.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in HPEB 502 or equivalent.
HPEB 752.subject: HPEB
HPEB 752.title: Nutrition and Public Health

HPEB 753.description: The public health implications of obesity and eating disorders, considerations of causes, and intervention strategies.
HPEB 753.subject: HPEB
HPEB 753.title: Obesity and Eating Disorders

HPEB 754.description: Role of the physical activity specialist within the community health department. Development, initiation, and evaluation of campaigns, resources, community capacity building, and coalitions to promote physical activity.
HPEB 754.subject: HPEB
HPEB 754.title: Community-Based Physical Activity Intervention

HPEB 760.description: An overview of health education program models and strategies designed for workers in industry and business.
HPEB 760.subject: HPEB
HPEB 760.title: Health Education in Occupational Worksites

HPEB 769.description: Current knowledge about child abuse and neglect, including typologies, etiology, effects, and current practice interventions.
HPEB 769.subject: HPEB
HPEB 769.title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives on Child Abuse and Neglect

HPEB 771.description: Theories, measurement, and empirical evidence regarding structural factors and health. How social, economic, and environmental conditions can constrain and promote population and individual health.
HPEB 771.subject: HPEB
HPEB 771.title: Social Determinants of Health

HPEB 772.description: Selected global health challenges are used to examine sociopolitical, advocacy, policy, organizational, and programmatic actions by governmental, non-governmental, and international institutions aiming to improve health in resource-limited settings.
HPEB 772.subject: HPEB
HPEB 772.title: Responding to Global Health Challenges

HPEB 773.description: Various lecturers address the state of the art of public health strategies for third world countries aimed at the reduction of death and disease. Repeatable up to a maximum of 3 credit hours.
HPEB 773.subject: HPEB
HPEB 773.title: International Public Health Seminar

HPEB 775.description: Current health issues and needs of populations affected by humanitarian crises, and the role of humanitarian interventions in responding to those needs.
HPEB 775.subject: HPEB
HPEB 775.title: Health of Populations Affected by Humanitarian Crises

HPEB 779.description: Etiology of injuries and strategies for their prevention are examined within an interdisciplinary framework.
HPEB 779.subject: HPEB
HPEB 779.title: Injury Prevention and Control

HPEB 782A.description: Application of effective teaching techniques and organization of instructional settings in health for K-12.
HPEB 782A.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: acceptance to the Professional Program in Education.
HPEB 782A.subject: HPEB
HPEB 782A.title: Teaching Internship (Health)

HPEB 782B.description: Application of effective teaching techniques and organization of instructional settings in health for K-12.
HPEB 782B.subject: HPEB
HPEB 782B.title: Teaching Internship (Health)

HPEB 792.description: A study of selected issues confronted in health education programs.
HPEB 792.subject: HPEB
HPEB 792.title: Selected Topics in Health Education

HPEB 796.description: Performance of a predetermined work or service project in a health education setting.
HPEB 796.subject: HPEB
HPEB 796.title: Health Education Project

HPEB 797.description: The focus of this course is the synthesis and application of selected program learning objectives in the performance of an applied work or service project in a public need setting.
HPEB 797.subject: HPEB
HPEB 797.title: Applied Practice Experience

HPEB 798A.description: Synthesis and application of MPH competencies for professional development, culminating in a practicum fieldwork contract.
HPEB 798A.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: HPEB 700, HPEB 701, HPEB 702, HPEB 707, HPEB 710, HPEB 748.
HPEB 798A.subject: HPEB
HPEB 798A.title: Public Health Practicum Seminar

HPEB 798B.description: Performance of a limited work or service project in a public need setting, pursuit of planned, learning objectives related to previously identified aspects of the student's chosen role.
HPEB 798B.subject: HPEB
HPEB 798B.title: Public Health Practicum Fieldwork

HPEB 802.description: Implementation science aims to improve intervention effectiveness by studying the processes and activities around health program and policy implementation, incorporating knowledge and experiences of intervention implementers as well as of experts. Implementation science encompasses both general and intervention-specific research, centering implementation as the object of study.
HPEB 802.subject: HPEB
HPEB 802.title: Implementation Science of Health Promotion Interventions

HPEB 810.description: This doctoral seminar will examine conceptual and measurement issues regarding psychosocial constructs typically used in health education and health survey research--specifically health beliefs, health attitudes, health behaviors, health status, wellness, and perceptions of health care contexts.
HPEB 810.subject: HPEB
HPEB 810.title: Applied Measurement in Health Education Research

HPEB 811.description: Advanced conceptualization, development, and evaluation of communication strategies that aim to promote public health.
HPEB 811.subject: HPEB
HPEB 811.title: Advanced Public Health Communication: Theory and Methods

HPEB 815.description: Intermediate-level overview of methods for answering theoretically-informed research questions using quantitative data. Designed for applied researchers who seek a better understanding of statistical methods from describing a population to testing a conceptual model. Practical guidance for organizing, writing about, and presenting results from basic and multivariate statistical analyses.
HPEB 815.subject: HPEB
HPEB 815.title: Theory-Driven Analysis

HPEB 818.description: Evaluation methods including formative, retrospective and monitoring techniques; survey and trend analysis; application of experimental and quasi-experimental designs, triangulation, and cost-accounting.
HPEB 818.subject: HPEB
HPEB 818.title: Advanced Evaluation of Health Promotion Programs

HPEB 820.description: Overview of the key concepts and practices in advocacy efforts to promote the health of human populations through policy, including theories and conceptual frameworks for understanding how social and political change happens. Emphasis on strategies for promoting public health policies, and methods for evaluating advocacy activities and policy impacts.
HPEB 820.subject: HPEB
HPEB 820.title: Public Health Advocacy and Policy

HPEB 824.description: This advanced course examines issues related to planning, implementing or evaluating health promotion interventions that target change in physical and social including policy environments.
HPEB 824.subject: HPEB
HPEB 824.title: Social and Physical Environment Interventions in Health Promotion

HPEB 898.description: Applied comprehensive fieldwork experience which facilitates the synthesis of knowledge, skills and application of DrPH core competencies and core content of the discipline. Course may be taken a maximum of 3 times. Enrollment restricted to DrPH students.
HPEB 898.subject: HPEB
HPEB 898.title: Doctor of Public Health Practicum

HPEB 899.description: Prerequisite: one full year, 18 hrs, of graduate study beyond the master's level.
HPEB 899.subject: HPEB
HPEB 899.title: Dissertation Preparation
